title: Sisay activated the turn she lands, and the chain that grows her power

you: Sisay, Weatherlight Captain (cast this turn, has not attacked)
Derevi, Empyrial Tactician (entered two turns ago)
Bloom Tender (entered two turns ago, untapped)

stack.note: cost {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} already paid; the ability is on the stack and about to resolve

scenario.question: Sisay entered the battlefield this turn. (a) May she activate immediately, and why or why not? (b) What is Sisay's power before the first activation, and what is the exact set of mana values she may fetch? (c) If the first activation fetches Najeela, the Blade-Blossom, what is Sisay's power immediately afterward, and does the game recalculate it without any player taking an action? (d) With the remaining {W}{U}{B}{R}{G}, what is the largest mana value the second activation may fetch, and is Sheoldred, the Apocalypse a legal target for it? (e) At what point, if any, would Jodah, the Unifier become a legal fetch target?

steps.action: Answer (a). Sisay, Weatherlight Captain entered the battlefield this turn. Read her activation cost: everything before the colon is {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} — five mana, no {T} and no {Q} symbol.
steps.effect: She may activate immediately. The summoning-sickness rule restricts only (i) attacking and (ii) activated abilities whose activation cost contains the tap or untap symbol; it says nothing about mana-only costs. So Sisay can activate at any time she has priority on the turn she lands, once per {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} she can pay. Derevi, Empyrial Tactician and Bloom Tender have both been on the battlefield two turns and are unaffected by summoning sickness in any case.

steps.action: The response window on the second activation — the deck's real vulnerability. You pass priority; each opponent in turn order now has priority while the ability sits on the stack, and may cast instants or activate abilities before it resolves.
steps.effect: CORRECTION to the natural intuition: the fact that this ability has no targets does NOT make it safe. Not targeting only means the ability can never be countered on resolution for having an illegal target — the on-resolution legality check applies to spells and abilities that specify targets, and this one specifies none, so that check finds nothing to invalidate. It does not stop an opponent from changing the game state in response. Because the number is read at resolution (step 7), it can move DOWN as well as up during this window. Three concrete responses: (1) Kill Derevi. Other legendary permanents then reduce to Najeela alone (red, one color), Sisay's static bonus falls to +1/+1 and she is 3/3 when the ability resolves, so the search wants mana value less than 3. Sheoldred (4) and Jodah (5) are both now illegal finds, and nothing in the stated library qualifies — the ability resolves and finds nothing. This is the strongest answer. (2) Kill Najeela. Sisay is back to 5/5 and the ceiling reverts to mana value at most 4: Sheoldred is still legal, Jodah is not. (3) Remove Sisay herself — and here the answer depends on HOW. The ability resolves either way: once activated it exists on the stack independently of its source, and destruction or removal of the source after that time won't affect it. But the power it reads is not always 6. (3a) DESTROY, EXILE, BOUNCE or SACRIFICE (or any removal that changes her zone, and likewise lethal damage, which does not change her power at all): she is no longer in the public zone the effect expected her in, so the effect uses her last known information, which captures her last existence on the battlefield — base 2/2 with the +4/+4 from four colors still applied, power 6. The fetch ceiling is UNCHANGED at mana value 5, you still get Jodah, and the opponent has taken the commander without shrinking the search. (3b) A -X/-X EFFECT IS THE EXCEPTION, because a -X/-X is itself a layer 7c modification that is part of the power computation, whether or not she survives it. A -3/-3 leaves her on the battlefield at 3/3; she is still in the zone the effect expected her in, so the effect uses her CURRENT information — power 3, ceiling mana value less than 3, and neither Sheoldred nor Jodah can be found. A -6/-6 or larger drops her toughness to 0 or less, so she is put into her owner's graveyard as a state-based action; her last known information is her last existence on the battlefield, which includes that same -X/-X in layer 7c, giving a last known power of 0 and a ceiling of mana value less than 0 — no card qualifies. Against -X/-X removal, killing Sisay takes the commander AND shrinks the search. COACHING, conditioned on the removal type rather than stated flatly: against removal that changes her zone or deals damage — destroy, exile, bounce, sacrifice, burn, which is the common case — Derevi is the better target for an opponent than Sisay, because killing Derevi shrinks the search by three colors while killing Sisay leaves the ceiling at mana value 5. That ranking holds only for those answers. An opponent holding a -X/-X effect has no such dilemma: pointing it at Sisay takes the commander and shrinks the search in one card.

final_state.summary: Sisay activates twice the turn she lands. (a) Yes — her cost is {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} with no {T}, so summoning sickness is irrelevant. (b) She is 5/5 (base 2/2, +3/+3 for Derevi's green/white/blue), so activation one may find mana value 0-4 only; mana value 5 is excluded by the strict “less than.” (c) Finding Najeela adds red, making four colors, and Sisay becomes 6/6 automatically, mid-resolution, with no action, trigger or state-based action — a static ability's continuous effect is never locked in. (d) Activation two therefore reaches mana value 5; Sheoldred (mana value 4) is a legal choice, not a target. (e) Jodah (mana value 5) is illegal on activation one and becomes legal the instant Najeela enters during activation one's resolution, so activation two can take him. Best line shown: Najeela, then Jodah, leaving Sisay 11/11 with Jodah's anthem online. THE CAVEAT THAT MATTERS: because the power comparison is made at resolution, not at announcement, the ceiling can fall as well as rise. Each opponent gets priority while the second activation is on the stack; killing Derevi there drops Sisay to 3/3 and turns both Sheoldred and Jodah into illegal finds. Not targeting protects the ability from being countered for an illegal target; it protects nothing else. Killing Sisay in response is the weaker answer only against removal that changes her zone or deals damage — the ability resolves anyway on her last known power of 6. Against a -X/-X effect it is not weaker: the -X/-X is a layer 7c modification that is part of her power whether she survives it or dies to it, so that removal takes the commander and shrinks the search at the same time.

notes: Sisay's final power is an arithmetic decomposition, not a sequence of values: 2 (printed base) + 5 (her own ability, one for each of the five colors among other legendary permanents) + 4 (Jodah's anthem, one for each of the four legendary creatures you control) = 11. There is no moment at which she is 7. Her own +5/+5 and Jodah's +4/+4 are both layer 7c continuous effects that begin applying at the same instant Jodah enters; CR 613.7's timestamp system fixes the order in which the two are APPLIED within that sublayer, not a sequence of observable values, so from the instant Jodah enters she is 11/11. The only earlier values are the ones read by the two activations: 5 (2 + 3 for Derevi's green/white/blue) before activation one, and 6 (2 + 4 once Najeela adds red) for activation two.
Find ceilings: activation one = mana value at most 4; activation two = mana value at most 5 — but only if the board is unchanged when it resolves.
